title: Magnitude-type controls reversed a first-hour size contrast after shallow M7+ ComCat centers in 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether recorded M5.5+ events were more often M6+ in the first hour than on days 1-7 after large shallow earthquakes. We selected 232 M7+ centers in global ComCat data for 2001-2024. Within 200 km, 140 centers had 629 counted events. The within-center odds ratio was 0.64, with a 95% center bootstrap interval of 0.38-1.03. The planned positive test gave exact p = 0.949. Thus the primary test gave no first-hour excess. A planned check that held preferred magnitude type fixed reversed the ratio to 8.73 (2.39-39.84), but only 17 strata informed this check. Body-wave magnitude had a 77.5% share in the first hour and an 18.8% share on days 1-7. This size contrast depends on magnitude practice and sample support. It does not separate missing detections, scale choice and physical change. Code, aggregate counts, a figure, source hashes and an independent assignment audit are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: First-hour versus days 1-7 odds of the larger recorded size class. Lines show 95% center bootstrap intervals. Most checks use M5.5+ with a split at M6; floor60_cut65 uses M6+ with a split at M6.5. Type controls change sample support. Checks share records.
